title: Fourier neural operators for spatiotemporal dynamics in two-dimensional turbulence
problem: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent flows is computationally expensive for real-world applications, and existing machine learning approaches become unstable or produce unphysical results for long-term predictions.
motivation: Accelerating turbulence simulations while maintaining accuracy is critical for engineering and scientific applications requiring large-scale fluid dynamics predictions.
method: The approach combines Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) with PDE solvers to accelerate turbulence simulations. FNO models are trained on spatiotemporal data to learn the dynamics of 2D turbulent flows, treating them as equivalent to traditional PDE solvers. The method systematically investigates the required data volume and temporal resolution for effective pre-training and long-term stability.
key_novelty: Treating FNO models as equivalent PDE solvers and systematically determining the data requirements (volume and temporal resolution) for building stable, long-time turbulence prediction models.
contributions: FNO-based acceleration framework for turbulence DNS simulations
Systematic analysis of data volume and temporal resolution requirements for pre-trained turbulence models
Identification of key pitfalls in data-driven approaches affecting long-term stability and physical validity
Guidelines for making machine learning models competitive alternatives to traditional PDE solvers
limitations: Specific performance metrics and quantitative comparisons with baselines not detailed in abstract.
